blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
js:
README.md
agentDocGenerator.js
agentValidator.js
agentWorkflowGraph.js
aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter.js
assignForReview.js
assignForSolutionArchitecture.js
branchNaming
cacheToReleases.js
checkBugTestsPassed.js
checkBugToFixReady.js
checkStoryTestsPassed.js
checkSubtasksDoneForBA.js
checkTaskStoriesDone.js
checkWipLabel.js
checkoutBranch.js
closeQuestionTicket.js
commitAndPushToBaseBranch.js
common
config.js
configLoader.js
createBugFixBatchEpic.js
createIntakeTickets.js
createPlannedStoriesFromOutput.js
createQuestionsAndAssignForReview.js
createRepoTasks.js
createRepoTasksMulti.js
createSolutionDesignTicketsAndAssignForReview.js
developBugAndCreatePR.js
developBugFixBatchAndCreatePR.js
developTicketAndCreatePR.js

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
# 🚨 BLOCKING: the head is read from `ticket.pr.headSha`, which is `null` for PR-carrier rules — the entire gh-840 mechanism is inert in production

Both new code paths derive the head only from the query item:

```javascript

```

Neither consuming rule qualifies:

- `rework-on-label`: `{"type":"pr","labels":["agent:rework"]}` → `item.pr` stays `null`
- `rework-arm-restore` (this PR): `{"type":"pr","notLabels":["agent:rework"],"threadsResolved":false,"prMachineAuthor":true}` → `item.pr` stays `null` (`threadsResolved` reads threads via a separate provider probe; `prMachineAuthor` reads the free `item.author`)

Live consequences, all silent:

1. **No audit marker is ever posted.** With `head === null`, `buildConsumeAuditComment()` returns `null` and `auditReworkConsumption` hits `if (!body) return;` — no marker, no warning. ...

The ticket's AC2 close proof is "comment + head advanced **OR** explicit no-threads-to-own proof". This approximation treats *any* head move as the close marker — but `update_branch` (the silent git-merge refresh, js/smAgent.js `silentUpdateBranch`) pushes a merge commit to the PR head **without resolving review threads and without any rework leg running**. blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
js:
README.md
agentDocGenerator.js
agentValidator.js
agentWorkflowGraph.js
aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter.js
assignForReview.js
assignForSolutionArchitecture.js
branchNaming
cacheToReleases.js
checkBugTestsPassed.js
checkBugToFixReady.js
checkStoryTestsPassed.js
checkSubtasksDoneForBA.js
checkTaskStoriesDone.js
checkWipLabel.js
checkoutBranch.js

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
# 🚨 BLOCKING: the head is read from `ticket.pr.headSha`, which is `null` for PR-carrier rules — the entire gh-840 mechanism is inert in production

Both new code paths derive the head only from the query item:

```javascript

var head = reworkLatchHeadOf(ticket);                                       // restoreReworkArm
```

Neither consuming rule qualifies:

- `rework-on-label`: `{"type":"pr","labels":["agent:rework"]}` → `item.pr` stays `null`
- `rework-arm-restore` (this PR): `{"type":"pr","notLabels":["agent:rework"],"threadsResolved":false,"prMachineAuthor":true}` → `item.pr` stays `null` (`threadsResolved` reads threads via a separate provider probe; `prMachineAuthor` reads the free `item.author`)

Live consequences, all silent:

1. **No audit marker is ever posted.** With `head === null`, `buildConsumeAuditComment()` returns `null` and `auditReworkConsumption` hits `if (!body) return;` — no marker, no warning. # ⚠️ IMPORTANT: any head move is treated as a rework close — a silent branch refresh after a bogus consumption defeats the sweep permanently

```javascript

    String(newestConsume.head) !== String(head));
...

```

The ticket's AC2 close proof is "comment + head advanced **OR** explicit no-threads-to-own proof". This approximation treats *any* head move as the close marker — but `update_branch` (the silent git-merge refresh, js/smAgent.js `silentUpdateBranch`) pushes a merge commit to the PR head **without resolving review threads and without any rework leg running**. 1. bogus consumption of `agent:rework` (head `H1`, machine threads unresolved) → consume marker stamped for `H1`;

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
js:
README.md
agentDocGenerator.js
agentValidator.js
agentWorkflowGraph.js
aiTeammateTokenUsageReporter.js
assignForReview.js
assignForSolutionArchitecture.js
branchNaming
cacheToReleases.js
checkBugTestsPassed.js
checkBugToFixReady.js
checkStoryTestsPassed.js
checkSubtasksDoneForBA.js
checkTaskStoriesDone.js
checkWipLabel.js

Since `unresolvedMachineThreads > 0` is already required for restore and the sweep only runs when `threadsResolved: false`... Actually the simplest robust fix per suggestion: accept `head-advanced` as close proof only when corroborated by a concluded rework leg run on the current head with created_at at/after the consumption timestamp. The AC2 close proof per ticket is "comment + head advanced OR explicit no-threads-to-own proof". The reviewer suggests corroborating head-advanced with a concluded leg run on the current head at/after consumption time.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
# 🚨 BLOCKING: the head is read from `ticket.pr.headSha`, which is `null` for PR-carrier rules — the entire gh-840 mechanism is inert in production

Both new code paths derive the head only from the query item:

```javascript

```

Neither consuming rule qualifies:

- `rework-on-label`: `{"type":"pr","labels":["agent:rework"]}` → `item.pr` stays `null`
- `rework-arm-restore` (this PR): `{"type":"pr","notLabels":["agent:rework"],"threadsResolved":false,"prMachineAuthor":true}` → `item.pr` stays `null` (`threadsResolved` reads threads via a separate provider probe; `prMachineAuthor` reads the free `item.author`)

Live consequences, all silent:

1. **No audit marker is ever posted.** With `head === null`, `buildConsumeAuditComment()` returns `null` and `auditReworkConsumption` hits `if (!body) return;` — no marker, no warning. All CI checks passed on the rework head (or no check reported a failure).

- `ci_failures_full.log` will not exist when nothing failed.

  written once by rework setup at leg start.# pr-841: gh-840 [GOAL] agent:rework consumed WITHOUT the rework leg running — fail-open consumption hangs PRs (live: #826, 4h+ no fix commit, threads open, no close marker)

## Description

Closes #840
### Root Cause
- Live PR #826 (gh-825): `agent:rework` was consumed by the `rework-on-label` rule's `consumeLabels` path (dispatch accepted, or gh-715 cross-anchor suppression while a review leg held the other anchor) — yet no rework leg ever ran, no push, 4/6 threads open, no close marker.
- Consumption is fail-open: nothing records it, and every re-arm path (`arm_rework`) is withheld in this state (gh-806 latch, gh-807 verdict gate) — the PR hangs forever.

### Fix
- `js/common/reworkConsumption.js` (new): consumption-audit markers (path + head, machine-author-gated) and the pure `shouldRestoreArm` sweep decision.
- `js/smAgent.js`: both `consumeLabels` branches stamp a gh-840 audit comment on every `agent:rework` consumption; new `restore_rework_arm` localAction re-arms when a consumption is proven bogus (marker evidence, head not advanced, no rework in flight, quiet > `staleMinutes`).
- `sm_github.json`: new `rework-arm-restore` rule (machine PRs, unresolved threads, no label; `staleMinutes: 30` ≈ 6 ticks).

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `js/unit-tests/test_reworkConsumption.js` — 16 tests (marker protocol, AC1 restore, AC2 close proofs, AC3 human-only untouched, grace bound). Registered in `run_all.json`.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 9 integration tests replaying the #826 timeline (restore, grace, head-advanced, gh-807 gate preserved, human threads, in-flight leg, audit-on-consume, deployed-rule shape).
- Full suite: **2442 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

### Notes
- gh-807 verdict semantics untouched (non-goal); gh-744 preserved — the sweep counts only machine-authored unresolved threads and requires consumption evidence.
- AC4 (live metric) needs post-ship observation; the sweep self-heals the next occurrence ≤6 ticks by construction.

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #841._

> ℹ️ **1 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
# 🚨 BLOCKING: the head is read from `ticket.pr.headSha`, which is `null` for PR-carrier rules — the entire gh-840 mechanism is inert in production

Both new code paths derive the head only from the query item:

```javascript
var head = ((ticket.pr && ticket.pr.headSha) || ticket.headSha) || null;   // auditReworkConsumption
var head = reworkLatchHeadOf(ticket);                                       // restoreReworkArm
```

For PR-carrier rules, `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` builds items with **`pr: null`** and only populates `item.pr` when `needsStatus` is true — i.e. when the rule query carries `checks` / `mergeState` / `notMergeState` / `mergeable` / `prChecks` / `latestVerdict` / `notLatestVerdict` (see the `needsStatus` block and the gh-807 comment above it). Neither consuming rule qualifies:

- `rework-on-label`: `{"type":"pr","labels":["agent:rework"]}` → `item.pr` stays `null`
- `rework-arm-restore` (this PR): `{"type":"pr","notLabels":["agent:rework"],"threadsResolved":false,"prMachineAuthor":true}` → `item.pr` stays `null` (`threadsResolved` reads threads via a separate provider probe; `prMachineAuthor` reads the free `item.author`)

Live consequences, all silent:

1. **No audit marker is ever posted.** With `head === null`, `buildConsumeAuditComment()` returns `null` and `auditReworkConsumption` hits `if (!body) return;` — no marker, no warning. The ticket's "Audit log: every consumption records its path" capability never happens, and the sweep has no evidence to ever act on.
2. **The sweep's head-dependent gates are all dead.** `head === null` → `consultReworkLatch` short-circuits to not-latched (gh-806 latch bypassed), the `hasActiveLegRun` check is skipped entirely (in-flight legs don't block the restore), `headAdvanced` is always `false` (the AC2 "head advanced = close proof" branch never fires), the restore marker records head `'unknown'`, and `armReworkLatch(ticket)` no-ops — so after a restore there is no latch protecting against a stacked dispatch.

The 25 tests pass because every fixture injects `pr: { …, headSha: HEAD }` — a shape the live query layer never produces for these two rules. This is exactly the class of bug the tests were meant to exclude.

**Fix:** probe the head through the existing `prHeadAndLabels(repoInfo, ticket.prNumber)` helper (the same fresh-probe pattern `reworkArmGate` already uses at js/smAgent.js:4065) as a fallback in both `auditReworkConsumption` and `restoreReworkArm`, and log a warning when an `agent:rework` consumption cannot be attributed (fail loud, not `return;`). Add at least one test per path with the **live item shape** (`pr: null`) asserting the probe fallback — that test would have caught this.

Related pre-existing note (not this PR's scope, but it shares the same broken assumption): `arm_rework` (`rework-unresolved-threads`, query has no status keys either) also runs with `item.pr === null`, so its gh-806 latch consult/arm is equally inert on the PR-carrier path — worth a follow-up ticket, since it is one of the three "withheld re-arm" causes named in the gh-840 forensics.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: any head move is treated as a rework close — a silent branch refresh after a bogus consumption defeats the sweep permanently

```javascript
var headAdvanced = !!(newestConsume && newestConsume.head && head &&
    String(newestConsume.head) !== String(head));
...
headAdvancedPastConsumption: headAdvanced,
```

The ticket's AC2 close proof is "comment + head advanced **OR** explicit no-threads-to-own proof". This approximation treats *any* head move as the close marker — but `update_branch` (the silent git-merge refresh, js/smAgent.js `silentUpdateBranch`) pushes a merge commit to the PR head **without resolving review threads and without any rework leg running**. Timeline that breaks the sweep:

1. bogus consumption of `agent:rework` (head `H1`, machine threads unresolved) → consume marker stamped for `H1`;
2. the next refresh tick merges `main` → head advances to `H2`, threads untouched;
3. every subsequent sweep: `unresolvedMachineThreads > 0` but `headAdvanced === true` → `'head-advanced'` → **no restore, forever** — the exact consumed-without-work hang this PR exists to fix, now invisible to the recovery path.

The mitigating re-review loop (stale verdict → re-review → fresh verdict → `arm_rework`) may eventually recover such PRs, but gh-840's own forensics show review legs ran repeatedly on #826 for 4h+ without any re-arm landing — relying on that loop is what made the sweep necessary.

```javascript

    workspace: repoInfo.owner, repository: repoInfo.repo,
    pullRequestId: prNumber

  written once by rework setup at leg start.# pr-841: gh-840 [GOAL] agent:rework consumed WITHOUT the rework leg running — fail-open consumption hangs PRs (live: #826, 4h+ no fix commit, threads open, no close marker)

## Description

Closes #840
### Root Cause
- Live PR #826 (gh-825): `agent:rework` was consumed by the `rework-on-label` rule's `consumeLabels` path (dispatch accepted, or gh-715 cross-anchor suppression while a review leg held the other anchor) — yet no rework leg ever ran, no push, 4/6 threads open, no close marker.
- Consumption is fail-open: nothing records it, and every re-arm path (`arm_rework`) is withheld in this state (gh-806 latch, gh-807 verdict gate) — the PR hangs forever.

### Fix
- `js/common/reworkConsumption.js` (new): consumption-audit markers (path + head, machine-author-gated) and the pure `shouldRestoreArm` sweep decision.
- `js/smAgent.js`: both `consumeLabels` branches stamp a gh-840 audit comment on every `agent:rework` consumption; new `restore_rework_arm` localAction re-arms when a consumption is proven bogus (marker evidence, head not advanced, no rework in flight, quiet > `staleMinutes`).
- `sm_github.json`: new `rework-arm-restore` rule (machine PRs, unresolved threads, no label; `staleMinutes: 30` ≈ 6 ticks).

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `js/unit-tests/test_reworkConsumption.js` — 16 tests (marker protocol, AC1 restore, AC2 close proofs, AC3 human-only untouched, grace bound). Registered in `run_all.json`.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 9 integration tests replaying the #826 timeline (restore, grace, head-advanced, gh-807 gate preserved, human threads, in-flight leg, audit-on-consume, deployed-rule shape).
- Full suite: **2442 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

### Notes
- gh-807 verdict semantics untouched (non-goal); gh-744 preserved — the sweep counts only machine-authored unresolved threads and requires consumption evidence.
- AC4 (live metric) needs post-ship observation; the sweep self-heals the next occurrence ≤6 ticks by construction.

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

## Description

Closes #840
### Root Cause
- Live PR #826 (gh-825): `agent:rework` was consumed by the `rework-on-label` rule's `consumeLabels` path (dispatch accepted, or gh-715 cross-anchor suppression while a review leg held the other anchor) — yet no rework leg ever ran, no push, 4/6 threads open, no close marker.
- Consumption is fail-open: nothing records it, and every re-arm path (`arm_rework`) is withheld in this state (gh-806 latch, gh-807 verdict gate) — the PR hangs forever.

### Fix
- `js/common/reworkConsumption.js` (new): consumption-audit markers (path + head, machine-author-gated) and the pure `shouldRestoreArm` sweep decision.
- `js/smAgent.js`: both `consumeLabels` branches stamp a gh-840 audit comment on every `agent:rework` consumption; new `restore_rework_arm` localAction re-arms when a consumption is proven bogus (marker evidence, head not advanced, no rework in flight, quiet > `staleMinutes`).
- `sm_github.json`: new `rework-arm-restore` rule (machine PRs, unresolved threads, no label; `staleMinutes: 30` ≈ 6 ticks).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

Now I understand the code. Three threads to fix:

**Thread 1 (BLOCKING)**: head read from `ticket.pr.headSha`/`ticket.headSha` which is `null` for PR-carrier rules. Fix: probe via `prHeadAndLabels(repoInfo, ticket.prNumber)` fallback in both `auditReworkConsumption` and `restoreReworkArm`, warn when consumption can't be attributed. Add tests with live item shape `pr: null`.

**Thread 2 (IMPORTANT)**: headAdvanced treats any head move as close proof. Fix: corroborate — e.g. require a concluded leg run on the current head at/after the consumption timestamp, OR fall through to restore when unresolved machine threads exist on the advanced head. Since `unresolvedMachineThreads > 0` is already required for restore and the sweep only runs when `threadsResolved: false`... Actually the simplest robust fix per suggestion: accept `head-advanced` as close proof only when corroborated by a concluded rework leg run on the current head with created_at at/after the consumption timestamp. Otherwise, if machine threads remain unresolved, treat as not head-advanced (fall through to restore). Also document in sm_github.json rule description.

Wait — the shouldRestoreArm pure function takes `headAdvancedPastConsumption`. I could compute a corroborated value in smAgent: `headAdvanced && !corroboratedByLegRun`. But then a genuinely closed rework (push + threads resolved) → machineThreads would be 0 → 'no-unresolved-threads'. Hmm, but what if rework pushed and resolved SOME threads but not all? The AC2 close proof per ticket is "comment + head advanced OR explicit no-threads-to-own proof". The reviewer suggests corroborating head-advanced with a concluded leg run on the current head at/after consumption time.

Simplest approach: compute `headAdvancedCloseProof = headAdvanced && hasConcludedLegRunOnHeadAfter(runs, head, consumedAtMs)`. We already fetch `headWorkflowRunsSafe(repoInfo, head)` for the active-leg check only when head is non-null. Let me restructure restoreReworkArm:

...
var headAdvanced = ...;
// gh-841 review: corroborate
var headCloseProven = headAdvanced && hasConcludedLegRunAtOrAfter(runs, consumedAtMs);
```

And pass `headAdvancedPastConsumption: headCloseProven` to shouldRestoreArm. Then if head advanced but no leg run corroboration, sweep proceeds to restore if threads are open and quiet — which matches "fall through to restore when unresolved machine threads still exist on the advanced head".

arguments.content:
## Fixed — head now probed via `prHeadAndLabels`, audit fails loud

Both new code paths no longer rely on the query item's `headSha` (which is `null` for PR-carrier rules since `queryPrs` populates `item.pr` only under `needsStatus`):

- **`auditReworkConsumption`** (`js/smAgent.js`): falls back to the fresh `prHeadAndLabels(repoInfo, ticket.prNumber)` probe (the same pattern `reworkArmGate` already uses) when the item carries no head. When the head still can't be attributed, it now logs a **warning** instead of the old silent `if (!body) return;` — the marker is the sweep's only consumption evidence, so a skipped audit must be loud.
- **`restoreReworkArm`** (`js/smAgent.js`): same probe fallback at the top of the sweep. An **unattributable head now fails closed** (warn + `return false`, retry next tick) — without a head we cannot prove the head did not advance past the consumed one, so restoring could re-arm an already-closed PR. The fetched head also feeds the active-leg-run check (previously dead when the item head was `null`), and the post-restore `armReworkLatch(ticket, head)` call now passes the probed head (`armReworkLatch` gained a `headOverride` parameter) so the restored arm actually gets the gh-806 stacked-dispatch protection instead of no-op'ing.

Tests added with the **live item shape** (`pr: null`), which would have caught this:

- `BLOCKING — audit log LIVE ITEM SHAPE …` — marker stamped with the probed head.
- `BLOCKING — audit log FAILS LOUD …` — probe failure → warning logged, no silent skip.
- `BLOCKING — sweep LIVE ITEM SHAPE …` — sweep restores on the live shape, marker records the probed head.
- `BLOCKING — sweep probe failure …` — no head anywhere → fail closed, no restore.

## Fixed — head-advanced is now a corroborated close proof; a silent refresh restores

`headAdvancedPastConsumption` no longer treats *any* head move as the AC2 close proof. New helper `hasConcludedLegRunAtOrAfter` (`js/smAgent.js`): the advanced head counts as close evidence **only when a concluded `ai-teammate.yml` leg run on the current head started at/after the consumption timestamp** — reusing the `headWorkflowRunsSafe` rollup already fetched for the in-flight check (no extra probe). Otherwise the sweep falls through to the restore check, so an advanced head with the same open machine threads (the `silentUpdateBranch` refresh shape) **restores the arm** instead of hiding the hang.

The deliberate tradeoff is documented in the `rework-arm-restore` rule description in `sm_github.json` (head provenance + head-advanced corroboration), so an incident review won't misread those restores as healthy closes.

Tests:

- `IMPORTANT — a SILENT refresh advanced the head with machine threads still open and no leg run → the sweep restores (refresh ≠ close)` — the exact timeline from this thread now re-arms.
- The existing `AC2 — head advanced …` test now supplies a concluded leg run on the advanced head (the corroborated close) and still expects no restore.

## Fixed — `pullRequestId` normalized to a string

`prCommentList` (`js/smAgent.js`) now passes `pullRequestId: String(prNumber)`, matching every sibling reader (`readVerdictRecords`, `smProvider.verdictRecords`, `prHeadAndLabels`, …). Since this PR also made the comment list the sweep's evidence source, a coercion difference would have silently returned zero markers — the fail-closed "no evidence" shape.

{"content":"## Fixed — head now probed via `prHeadAndLabels`, audit fails loud

Both new code paths no longer rely on the query item's `headSha` (which is `null` for PR-carrier rules since `queryPrs` populates `item.pr` only under `needsStatus`):

- **`auditReworkConsumption`** (`js/smAgent.js`): falls back to the fresh `prHeadAndLabels(repoInfo, ticket.prNumber)` probe (the same pattern `reworkArmGate` already uses) when the item carries no head. When the head still can't be attributed, it now logs a **warning** instead of the old silent `if (!body) return;` — the marker is the sweep's only consumption evidence, so a skipped audit must be loud.
- **`restoreReworkArm`** (`js/smAgent.js`): same probe fallback at the top of the sweep. An **unattributable head now fails closed** (warn + `return false`, retry next tick) — without a head we cannot prove the head did not advance past the consumed one, so restoring could re-arm an already-closed PR. The fetched head also feeds the active-leg-run check (previously dead when the item head was `null`), and the post-restore `armReworkLatch(ticket, head)` call now passes the probed head (`armReworkLatch` gained a `headOverride` parameter) so the restored arm actually gets the gh-806 stacked-dispatch protection instead of no-op'ing.

Tests added with the **live item shape** (`pr: null`), which would have caught this:

- `BLOCKING — audit log LIVE ITEM SHAPE …` — marker stamped with the probed head.
- `BLOCKING — audit log FAILS LOUD …` — probe failure → warning logged, no silent skip.
- `BLOCKING — sweep LIVE ITEM SHAPE …` — sweep restores on the live shape, marker records the probed head.
- `BLOCKING — sweep probe failure …` — no head anywhere → fail closed, no restore.

{"content":"## Fixed — head-advanced is now a corroborated close proof; a silent refresh restores

`headAdvancedPastConsumption` no longer treats *any* head move as the AC2 close proof. New helper `hasConcludedLegRunAtOrAfter` (`js/smAgent.js`): the advanced head counts as close evidence **only when a concluded `ai-teammate.yml` leg run on the current head started at/after the consumption timestamp** — reusing the `headWorkflowRunsSafe` rollup already fetched for the in-flight check (no extra probe). Otherwise the sweep falls through to the restore check, so an advanced head with the same open machine threads (the `silentUpdateBranch` refresh shape) **restores the arm** instead of hiding the hang.

The deliberate tradeoff is documented in the `rework-arm-restore` rule description in `sm_github.json` (head provenance + head-advanced corroboration), so an incident review won't misread those restores as healthy closes.

Both new code paths no longer rely on the query item's `headSha` (which is `null` for PR-carrier rules since `queryPrs` populates `item.pr` only under `needsStatus`):

- **`auditReworkConsumption`** (`js/smAgent.js`): falls back to the fresh `prHeadAndLabels(repoInfo, ticket.prNumber)` probe (the same pattern `reworkArmGate` already uses) when the item carries no head. When the head still can't be attributed, it now logs a **warning** instead of the old silent `if (!body) return;` — the marker is the sweep's only consumption evidence, so a skipped audit must be loud.
- **`restoreReworkArm`** (`js/smAgent.js`): same probe fallback at the top of the sweep. An **unattributable head now fails closed** (warn + `return false`, retry next tick) — without a head we cannot prove the head did not advance past the consumed one, so restoring could re-arm an already-closed PR. The fetched head also feeds the active-leg-run check (previously dead when the item head was `null`), and the post-restore `armReworkLatch(ticket, head)` call now passes the probed head (`armReworkLatch` gained a `headOverride` parameter) so the restored arm actually gets the gh-806 stacked-dispatch protection instead of no-op'ing.

Tests added with the **live item shape** (`pr: null`), which would have caught this:

- `BLOCKING — audit log LIVE ITEM SHAPE …` — marker stamped with the probed head.
- `BLOCKING — audit log FAILS LOUD …` — probe failure → warning logged, no silent skip.
- `BLOCKING — sweep LIVE ITEM SHAPE …` — sweep restores on the live shape, marker records the probed head.
- `BLOCKING — sweep probe failure …` — no head anywhere → fail closed, no restore.

{"content":"## Fixed — head-advanced is now a corroborated close proof; a silent refresh restores

`headAdvancedPastConsumption` no longer treats *any* head move as the AC2 close proof. New helper `hasConcludedLegRunAtOrAfter` (`js/smAgent.js`): the advanced head counts as close evidence **only when a concluded `ai-teammate.yml` leg run on the current head started at/after the consumption timestamp** — reusing the `headWorkflowRunsSafe` rollup already fetched for the in-flight check (no extra probe). Otherwise the sweep falls through to the restore check, so an advanced head with the same open machine threads (the `silentUpdateBranch` refresh shape) **restores the arm** instead of hiding the hang.

The deliberate tradeoff is documented in the `rework-arm-restore` rule description in `sm_github.json` (head provenance + head-advanced corroboration), so an incident review won't misread those restores as healthy closes.

Tests:

- `IMPORTANT — a SILENT refresh advanced the head with machine threads still open and no leg run → the sweep restores (refresh ≠ close)` — the exact timeline from this thread now re-arms.
- The existing `AC2 — head advanced …` test now supplies a concluded leg run on the advanced head (the corroborated close) and still expects no restore.

{"content":"## Fixed — head now probed via `prHeadAndLabels`, audit fails loud

Both new code paths no longer rely on the query item's `headSha` (which is `null` for PR-carrier rules since `queryPrs` populates `item.pr` only under `needsStatus`):

When the head still can't be attributed, it now logs a **warning** instead of the old silent `if (!body) return;` — the marker is the sweep's only consumption evidence, so a skipped audit must be loud.
- **`restoreReworkArm`** (`js/smAgent.js`): same probe fallback at the top of the sweep. An **unattributable head now fails closed** (warn + `return false`, retry next tick) — without a head we cannot prove the head did not advance past the consumed one, so restoring could re-arm an already-closed PR. The fetched head also feeds the active-leg-run check (previously dead when the item head was `null`), and the post-restore `armReworkLatch(ticket, head)` call now passes the probed head (`armReworkLatch` gained a `headOverride` parameter) so the restored arm actually gets the gh-806 stacked-dispatch protection instead of no-op'ing.

- **Thread 1 (🚨 BLOCKING)** — both gh-840 code paths derived the head from `ticket.pr.headSha`, which is `null` for PR-carrier rules (`queryPrs` populates `item.pr` only under `needsStatus`). The mechanism was inert in production: no audit markers, dead latch/active-run/head-advanced gates.
- **Thread 2 (⚠️ IMPORTANT)** — any head move counted as the AC2 "close proof", so a silent `silentUpdateBranch` refresh after a bogus consumption suppressed the sweep forever with machine threads still open.
- **Thread 3 (💡 SUGGESTION)** — `prCommentList` passed `pullRequestId: prNumber` unstringified, unlike every sibling reader.
- Threads 4 and 5 in `pr_discussions_raw.json` carry `threadId: null` / `rootCommentId: null` — they are top-level PR comments, not resolvable review threads. Thread 5 is the gh-807 verdict record ("Do not edit or reply"). Thread 4 is the automated review summary whose three findings map 1:1 to threads 1–3 (fixed and replied above), so no separate threaded reply is possible for it.
- The reviewer's "Next step 4" (`arm_rework` sharing the null-`item.pr` assumption) is explicitly out of this PR's scope — a follow-up ticket, noted here.

## Approach

1. **Head provenance (BLOCKING)**: `auditReworkConsumption` and `restoreReworkArm` now fall back to the existing fresh-probe helper `prHeadAndLabels(repoInfo, ticket.prNumber)` (the same pattern `reworkArmGate` uses) when the query item carries no head. The audit path **fails loud** — an unattributable consumption logs a warning instead of silently skipping. The sweep **fails closed** on an unattributable head (no restore — without a head we can't prove it didn't advance past the consumed one).
2. **Latch protection restored**: `armReworkLatch(ticket, headOverride)` gained a head parameter so the post-restore gh-806 latch arms on the probed head instead of no-op'ing on the PR-carrier item shape.
3. **Corroborated head-advanced (IMPORTANT)**: new `hasConcludedLegRunAtOrAfter(runs, workflowFile, sinceMs)` helper — an advanced head is the close proof only when a **concluded `ai-teammate.yml` run on the current head started at/after the consumption** (reuses the already-fetched `headWorkflowRunsSafe` rollup). Otherwise the sweep falls through to the restore check, so a refresh-shaped advanced head with open machine threads re-arms. The tradeoff is documented in the `rework-arm-restore` rule description in `sm_github.json` as requested.
4. **String parity (SUGGESTION)**: `prCommentList` passes `pullRequestId: String(prNumber)`.

## Files Modified

- `js/smAgent.js` — probe fallback + fail-loud audit; probe fallback + fail-closed sweep; `hasConcludedLegRunAtOrAfter` (new, exported); `armReworkLatch` head override; `String(prNumber)` in `prCommentList`.
- `sm_github.json` — `rework-arm-restore` rule description documents head provenance and the corroborated head-advanced semantics.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 5 tests (see below); the AC2 head-advanced test now models the corroborated close proof.

## Test Coverage

RED first: the 4 new failing scenarios below were added and confirmed red against the pre-fix code, then turned green by the fix.

- `IMPORTANT — a SILENT refresh advanced the head with machine threads still open and no leg run → the sweep restores (refresh ≠ close)` — the exact defeating timeline from thread 2.
- `AC2 — head advanced …` updated: advanced head **+ concluded leg run** corroboration → still no restore.
- `BLOCKING — audit log LIVE ITEM SHAPE` (`pr: null` item) → marker stamped with the probed head.
- `BLOCKING — audit log FAILS LOUD` (probe fails) → warning logged, no marker, no silent skip.
- `BLOCKING — sweep LIVE ITEM SHAPE` (`pr: null` item) → arm restored, marker records the probed head.
- `BLOCKING — sweep probe failure` → fail closed, no restore, no crash.

Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` → **2447 passed, 0 failed** (was 2442 before this round; +5 new tests).

{"content":"## Fixed — head now probed via `prHeadAndLabels`, audit fails loud

Both new code paths no longer rely on the query item's `headSha` (which is `null` for PR-carrier rules since `queryPrs` populates `item.pr` only under `needsStatus`):

When the head still can't be attributed, it now logs a **warning** instead of the old silent `if (!body) return;` — the marker is the sweep's only consumption evidence, so a skipped audit must be loud.
- **`restoreReworkArm`** (`js/smAgent.js`): same probe fallback at the top of the sweep. An **unattributable head now fails closed** (warn + `return false`, retry next tick) — without a head we cannot prove the head did not advance past the consumed one, so restoring could re-arm an already-closed PR. The fetched head also feeds the active-leg-run check (previously dead when the item head was `null`), and the post-restore `armReworkLatch(ticket, head)` call now passes the probed head (`armReworkLatch` gained a `headOverride` parameter) so the restored arm actually gets the gh-806 stacked-dispatch protection instead of no-op'ing.

{"content":"# Rework round 1 — all open review threads addressed

## Issues/Notes

- **Thread 1 (🚨 BLOCKING)** — both gh-840 code paths derived the head from `ticket.pr.headSha`, which is `null` for PR-carrier rules (`queryPrs` populates `item.pr` only under `needsStatus`). The mechanism was inert in production: no audit markers, dead latch/active-run/head-advanced gates.
- **Thread 2 (⚠️ IMPORTANT)** — any head move counted as the AC2 "close proof", so a silent `silentUpdateBranch` refresh after a bogus consumption suppressed the sweep forever with machine threads still open.
- **Thread 3 (💡 SUGGESTION)** — `prCommentList` passed `pullRequestId: prNumber` unstringified, unlike every sibling reader.
- Threads 4 and 5 in `pr_discussions_raw.json` carry `threadId: null` / `rootCommentId: null` — they are top-level PR comments, not resolvable review threads. Thread 5 is the gh-807 verdict record ("Do not edit or reply"). Thread 4 is the automated review summary whose three findings map 1:1 to threads 1–3 (fixed and replied above), so no separate threaded reply is possible for it.
- The reviewer's "Next step 4" (`arm_rework` sharing the null-`item.pr` assumption) is explicitly out of this PR's scope — a follow-up ticket, noted here.

## Approach

1. **Head provenance (BLOCKING)**: `auditReworkConsumption` and `restoreReworkArm` now fall back to the existing fresh-probe helper `prHeadAndLabels(repoInfo, ticket.prNumber)` (the same pattern `reworkArmGate` uses) when the query item carries no head. The audit path **fails loud** — an unattributable consumption logs a warning instead of silently skipping. The sweep **fails closed** on an unattributable head (no restore — without a head we can't prove it didn't advance past the consumed one).
2. **Latch protection restored**: `armReworkLatch(ticket, headOverride)` gained a head parameter so the post-restore gh-806 latch arms on the probed head instead of no-op'ing on the PR-carrier item shape.
3. **Corroborated head-advanced (IMPORTANT)**: new `hasConcludedLegRunAtOrAfter(runs, workflowFile, sinceMs)` helper — an advanced head is the close proof only when a **concluded `ai-teammate.yml` run on the current head started at/after the consumption** (reuses the already-fetched `headWorkflowRunsSafe` rollup). Otherwise the sweep falls through to the restore check, so a refresh-shaped advanced head with open machine threads re-arms. The tradeoff is documented in the `rework-arm-restore` rule description in `sm_github.json` as requested.
4. **String parity (SUGGESTION)**: `prCommentList` passes `pullRequestId: String(prNumber)`.

{"content":"## Fixed — head now probed via `prHeadAndLabels`, audit fails loud

Both new code paths no longer rely on the query item's `headSha` (which is `null` for PR-carrier rules since `queryPrs` populates `item.pr` only under `needsStatus`):

- **`auditReworkConsumption`** (`js/smAgent.js`): falls back to the fresh `prHeadAndLabels(repoInfo, ticket.prNumber)` probe (the same pattern `reworkArmGate` already uses) when the item carries no head. When the head still can't be attributed, it now logs a **warning** instead of the old silent `if (!body) return;` — the marker is the sweep's only consumption evidence, so a skipped audit must be loud.
- **`restoreReworkArm`** (`js/smAgent.js`): same probe fallback at the top of the sweep. An **unattributable head now fails closed** (warn + `return false`, retry next tick) — without a head we cannot prove the head did not advance past the consumed one, so restoring could re-arm an already-closed PR. The fetched head also feeds the active-leg-run check (previously dead when the item head was `null`), and the post-restore `armReworkLatch(ticket, head)` call now passes the probed head (`armReworkLatch` gained a `headOverride` parameter) so the restored arm actually gets the gh-806 stacked-dispatch protection instead of no-op'ing.

- `BLOCKING — sweep probe failure …` — no head anywhere → fail closed, no restore.

Both new code paths no longer rely on the query item's `headSha` (which is `null` for PR-carrier rules since `queryPrs` populates `item.pr` only under `needsStatus`):

An **unattributable head now fails closed** (warn + `return false`, retry next tick) — without a head we cannot prove the head did not advance past the consumed one, so restoring could re-arm an already-closed PR. {"content":"## Fixed — head now probed via `prHeadAndLabels`, audit fails loud

Both new code paths no longer rely on the query item's `headSha` (which is `null` for PR-carrier rules since `queryPrs` populates `item.pr` only under `needsStatus`):

- **`auditReworkConsumption`** (`js/smAgent.js`): falls back to the fresh `prHeadAndLabels(repoInfo, ticket.prNumber)` probe (the same pattern `reworkArmGate` already uses) when the item carries no head. When the head still can't be attributed, it now logs a **warning** instead of the old silent `if (!body) return;` — the marker is the sweep's only consumption evidence, so a skipped audit must be loud.
- **`restoreReworkArm`** (`js/smAgent.js`): same probe fallback at the top of the sweep. An **unattributable head now fails closed** (warn + `return false`, retry next tick) — without a head we cannot prove the head did not advance past the consumed one, so restoring could re-arm an already-closed PR. The fetched head also feeds the active-leg-run check (previously dead when the item head was `null`), and the post-restore `armReworkLatch(ticket, head)` call now passes the probed head (`armReworkLatch` gained a `headOverride` parameter) so the restored arm actually gets the gh-806 stacked-dispatch protection instead of no-op'ing.

Tests added with the **live item shape** (`pr: null`), which would have caught this:

- `BLOCKING — audit log LIVE ITEM SHAPE …` — marker stamped with the probed head.
- `BLOCKING — audit log FAILS LOUD …` — probe failure → warning logged, no silent skip.
- `BLOCKING — sweep LIVE ITEM SHAPE …` — sweep restores on the live shape, marker records the probed head.
- `BLOCKING — sweep probe failure …` — no head anywhere → fail closed, no restore.

{"content":"# Rework round 1 — all open review threads addressed

## Issues/Notes

- **Thread 1 (🚨 BLOCKING)** — both gh-840 code paths derived the head from `ticket.pr.headSha`, which is `null` for PR-carrier rules (`queryPrs` populates `item.pr` only under `needsStatus`). The mechanism was inert in production: no audit markers, dead latch/active-run/head-advanced gates.
- **Thread 2 (⚠️ IMPORTANT)** — any head move counted as the AC2 "close proof", so a silent `silentUpdateBranch` refresh after a bogus consumption suppressed the sweep forever with machine threads still open.
- **Thread 3 (💡 SUGGESTION)** — `prCommentList` passed `pullRequestId: prNumber` unstringified, unlike every sibling reader.
- Threads 4 and 5 in `pr_discussions_raw.json` carry `threadId: null` / `rootCommentId: null` — they are top-level PR comments, not resolvable review threads. Thread 5 is the gh-807 verdict record ("Do not edit or reply"). Thread 4 is the automated review summary whose three findings map 1:1 to threads 1–3 (fixed and replied above), so no separate threaded reply is possible for it.
- The reviewer's "Next step 4" (`arm_rework` sharing the null-`item.pr` assumption) is explicitly out of this PR's scope — a follow-up ticket, noted here.

## Approach

1. **Head provenance (BLOCKING)**: `auditReworkConsumption` and `restoreReworkArm` now fall back to the existing fresh-probe helper `prHeadAndLabels(repoInfo, ticket.prNumber)` (the same pattern `reworkArmGate` uses) when the query item carries no head. The audit path **fails loud** — an unattributable consumption logs a warning instead of silently skipping. The sweep **fails closed** on an unattributable head (no restore — without a head we can't prove it didn't advance past the consumed one).
2. **Latch protection restored**: `armReworkLatch(ticket, headOverride)` gained a head parameter so the post-restore gh-806 latch arms on the probed head instead of no-op'ing on the PR-carrier item shape.
3. **Corroborated head-advanced (IMPORTANT)**: new `hasConcludedLegRunAtOrAfter(runs, workflowFile, sinceMs)` helper — an advanced head is the close proof only when a **concluded `ai-teammate.yml` run on the current head started at/after the consumption** (reuses the already-fetched `headWorkflowRunsSafe` rollup). Otherwise the sweep falls through to the restore check, so a refresh-shaped advanced head with open machine threads re-arms. The tradeoff is documented in the `rework-arm-restore` rule description in `sm_github.json` as requested.
4. **String parity (SUGGESTION)**: `prCommentList` passes `pullRequestId: String(prNumber)`.

## Files Modified

- `js/smAgent.js` — probe fallback + fail-loud audit; probe fallback + fail-closed sweep; `hasConcludedLegRunAtOrAfter` (new, exported); `armReworkLatch` head override; `String(prNumber)` in `prCommentList`.

{"content":"## Fixed — head now probed via `prHeadAndLabels`, audit fails loud

Both new code paths no longer rely on the query item's `headSha` (which is `null` for PR-carrier rules since `queryPrs` populates `item.pr` only under `needsStatus`):

- **`auditReworkConsumption`** (`js/smAgent.js`): falls back to the fresh `prHeadAndLabels(repoInfo, ticket.prNumber)` probe (the same pattern `reworkArmGate` already uses) when the item carries no head. When the head still can't be attributed, it now logs a **warning** instead of the old silent `if (!body) return;` — the marker is the sweep's only consumption evidence, so a skipped audit must be loud.
- **`restoreReworkArm`** (`js/smAgent.js`): same probe fallback at the top of the sweep. An **unattributable head now fails closed** (warn + `return false`, retry next tick) — without a head we cannot prove the head did not advance past the consumed one, so restoring could re-arm an already-closed PR. The fetched head also feeds the active-leg-run check (previously dead when the item head was `null`), and the post-restore `armReworkLatch(ticket, head)` call now passes the probed head (`armReworkLatch` gained a `headOverride` parameter) so the restored arm actually gets the gh-806 stacked-dispatch protection instead of no-op'ing.

- **`restoreReworkArm`** (`js/smAgent.js`): same probe fallback at the top of the sweep. An **unattributable head now fails closed** (warn + `return false`, retry next tick) — without a head we cannot prove the head did not advance past the consumed one, so restoring could re-arm an already-closed PR. The fetched head also feeds the active-leg-run check (previously dead when the item head was `null`), and the post-restore `armReworkLatch(ticket, head)` call now passes the probed head (`armReworkLatch` gained a `headOverride` parameter) so the restored arm actually gets the gh-806 stacked-dispatch protection instead of no-op'ing.

- **`restoreReworkArm`** (`js/smAgent.js`): same probe fallback at the top of the sweep. An **unattributable head now fails closed** (warn + `return false`, retry next tick) — without a head we cannot prove the head did not advance past the consumed one, so restoring could re-arm an already-closed PR. The fetched head also feeds the active-leg-run check (previously dead when the item head was `null`), and the post-restore `armReworkLatch(ticket, head)` call now passes the probed head (`armReworkLatch` gained a `headOverride` parameter) so the restored arm actually gets the gh-806 stacked-dispatch protection instead of no-op'ing.

{"content":"## Fixed — head now probed via `prHeadAndLabels`, audit fails loud

Both new code paths no longer rely on the query item's `headSha` (which is `null` for PR-carrier rules since `queryPrs` populates `item.pr` only under `needsStatus`):

- **`auditReworkConsumption`** (`js/smAgent.js`): falls back to the fresh `prHeadAndLabels(repoInfo, ticket.prNumber)` probe (the same pattern `reworkArmGate` already uses) when the item carries no head. When the head still can't be attributed, it now logs a **warning** instead of the old silent `if (!body) return;` — the marker is the sweep's only consumption evidence, so a skipped audit must be loud.

{"content":"## Fixed — head now probed via `prHeadAndLabels`, audit fails loud

Both new code paths no longer rely on the query item's `headSha` (which is `null` for PR-carrier rules since `queryPrs` populates `item.pr` only under `needsStatus`):

- **`auditReworkConsumption`** (`js/smAgent.js`): falls back to the fresh `prHeadAndLabels(repoInfo, ticket.prNumber)` probe (the same pattern `reworkArmGate` already uses) when the item carries no head. When the head still can't be attributed, it now logs a **warning** instead of the old silent `if (!body) return;` — the marker is the sweep's only consumption evidence, so a skipped audit must be loud.
- **`restoreReworkArm`** (`js/smAgent.js`): same probe fallback at the top of the sweep. An **unattributable head now fails closed** (warn + `return false`, retry next tick) — without a head we cannot prove the head did not advance past the consumed one, so restoring could re-arm an already-closed PR. The fetched head also feeds the active-leg-run check (previously dead when the item head was `null`), and the post-restore `armReworkLatch(ticket, head)` call now passes the probed head (`armReworkLatch` gained a `headOverride` parameter) so the restored arm actually gets the gh-806 stacked-dispatch protection instead of no-op'ing.

Tests added with the **live item shape** (`pr: null`), which would have caught this:

- `BLOCKING — audit log LIVE ITEM SHAPE …` — marker stamped with the probed head.
- `BLOCKING — audit log FAILS LOUD …` — probe failure → warning logged, no silent skip.
- `BLOCKING — sweep LIVE ITEM SHAPE …` — sweep restores on the live shape, marker records the probed head.
- `BLOCKING — sweep probe failure …` — no head anywhere → fail closed, no restore.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md"}

{"content":"## Fixed — head-advanced is now a corroborated close proof; a silent refresh restores

`headAdvancedPastConsumption` no longer treats *any* head move as the AC2 close proof. New helper `hasConcludedLegRunAtOrAfter` (`js/smAgent.js`): the advanced head counts as close evidence **only when a concluded `ai-teammate.yml` leg run on the current head started at/after the consumption timestamp** — reusing the `headWorkflowRunsSafe` rollup already fetched for the in-flight check (no extra probe). Otherwise the sweep falls through to the restore check, so an advanced head with the same open machine threads (the `silentUpdateBranch` refresh shape) **restores the arm** instead of hiding the hang.

The deliberate tradeoff is documented in the `rework-arm-restore` rule description in `sm_github.json` (head provenance + head-advanced corroboration), so an incident review won't misread those restores as healthy closes.

Tests:

- `IMPORTANT — a SILENT refresh advanced the head with machine threads still open and no leg run → the sweep restores (refresh ≠ close)` — the exact timeline from this thread now re-arms.
- The existing `AC2 — head advanced …` test now supplies a concluded leg run on the advanced head (the corroborated close) and still expects no restore.

{"content":"# Rework round 1 — all open review threads addressed

## Issues/Notes

- **Thread 1 (🚨 BLOCKING)** — both gh-840 code paths derived the head from `ticket.pr.headSha`, which is `null` for PR-carrier rules (`queryPrs` populates `item.pr` only under `needsStatus`). The mechanism was inert in production: no audit markers, dead latch/active-run/head-advanced gates.
- **Thread 2 (⚠️ IMPORTANT)** — any head move counted as the AC2 "close proof", so a silent `silentUpdateBranch` refresh after a bogus consumption suppressed the sweep forever with machine threads still open.
- **Thread 3 (💡 SUGGESTION)** — `prCommentList` passed `pullRequestId: prNumber` unstringified, unlike every sibling reader.
- Threads 4 and 5 in `pr_discussions_raw.json` carry `threadId: null` / `rootCommentId: null` — they are top-level PR comments, not resolvable review threads. Thread 5 is the gh-807 verdict record ("Do not edit or reply"). Thread 4 is the automated review summary whose three findings map 1:1 to threads 1–3 (fixed and replied above), so no separate threaded reply is possible for it.

## Approach

2. **Latch protection restored**: `armReworkLatch(ticket, headOverride)` gained a head parameter so the post-restore gh-806 latch arms on the probed head instead of no-op'ing on the PR-carrier item shape.

Both new code paths no longer rely on the query item's `headSha` (which is `null` for PR-carrier rules since `queryPrs` populates `item.pr` only under `needsStatus`):

- **`restoreReworkArm`** (`js/smAgent.js`): same probe fallback at the top of the sweep. An **unattributable head now fails closed** (warn + `return false`, retry next tick) — without a head we cannot prove the head did not advance past the consumed one, so restoring could re-arm an already-closed PR. ## Fixed — head is probed via `prHeadAndLabels` on the live `pr: null` item shape; audit fails loud

Both gh-840 paths no longer rely on `ticket.pr.headSha` / `ticket.headSha` (always `null` for PR-carrier rules — `queryPrs` populates `item.pr` only under `needsStatus`, and neither `rework-on-label` nor `rework-arm-restore` qualifies):

- **`auditReworkConsumption`** (`js/smAgent.js`): when the item carries no head, it falls back to the fresh `prHeadAndLabels(repoInfo, ticket.prNumber)` probe (the same pattern `reworkArmGate` uses). When the head **still** can't be attributed, the skip is now a logged **warning**, not the old silent `if (!body) return;` — an unattributed consumption would leave the sweep without evidence forever.
- **`restoreReworkArm`** (`js/smAgent.js`): same probe fallback at the top of the sweep. The probed head is shared with `consultReworkLatch(key, ticket, repoInfo, head)` (new `headOverride` parameter — without it the latch consult short-circuited) and with `reworkArmGate(..., probeOverride)` (no double read). The active-leg-run gate now runs against the probed head instead of being skipped, the restore marker records the real head instead of `'unknown'`, and `armReworkLatch(ticket, head)` arms the gh-806 latch on the probed head (new `headOverride` parameter) so the restored arm gets stacked-dispatch protection instead of the arm no-op'ing.

Tests added with the **live item shape** (`pr: null`) — the shape that exposed this:

- `BLOCKING — audit path with the LIVE item shape (pr: null): the head is probed via prHeadAndLabels and stamped on the marker`
- `BLOCKING — audit path fails LOUD when the head cannot be attributed (pr: null, probe failed)`
- `BLOCKING — sweep with the LIVE item shape (pr: null): the head is probed and the arm is restored on it`
- `BLOCKING — sweep with the LIVE item shape (pr: null): an active leg run on the PROBED head suppresses the restore`

## Fixed — the head-position gate is gone; the close proof is thread ownership

`headAdvancedPastConsumption` has been **removed entirely** from the sweep (both the `restoreReworkArm` computation in `js/smAgent.js` and the `headAdvancedPastConsumption` input / `'head-advanced'` reason in `shouldRestoreArm`, `js/common/reworkConsumption.js`). Rationale, now documented in the module: a healthy close resolves the machine threads (`unresolvedMachineThreads === 0` → `'no-unresolved-threads'`), while a head move with the **same open machine threads** is a `silentUpdateBranch` refresh — never close evidence. So a bare head advance can no longer suppress the sweep; the exact timeline from this thread (bogus consumption → refresh merge advances the head → threads untouched → hang) now **restores the arm**, convergently and bounded by the grace window.

The tradeoff is documented where incident reviews will read it: the `rework-arm-restore` rule description in `sm_github.json` explicitly states that a bare head advance never suppresses the sweep, and that `'no-unresolved-threads'` / leg-in-flight are the healthy reads while an advanced head with open machine threads restores.

Tests:

- Pure module: `IMPORTANT — a head move with the same open machine threads is a refresh, not a close → restore`.
- The old AC2 head-advanced suppression expectation is gone from both suites — replaced by the census-driven close proof (`AC2 — nothing left to own (all machine threads resolved) → no restore` and the existing gh-807 gate tests still hold).
